To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we report FAM160B, with unknown function to be a novel gene for ID and that the disease in a 38-year-old female patient is characterized by microcephaly, ID, ataxia and behavioral abnormalities.
homozygous truncating variants in FAM160b1, an uncharacterized protein with unknown function, are associated with severe ID, speech problems and ataxia in an adult patient.
homozygous FAM160B‐deficiency causes ID, microcephalia, ataxia and behavioral problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel FAM160B gene and the clinical features of a new FAM160B‐related disorder.
the identification of a new ID syndrome, and the delineation of the clinical features of a new ID disorder.
the identification of a new syndrome, which we named as FAM160B‐1 syndrome, caused by homozygous FAM160B variant, and which we describe in detail.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FAM160A1‐related ID syndrome is characterized by severe ID, micro‐ or normocephaly, behavioral problems and speech problems.
FAM160‐associated syndromic ID is characterized by severe ID, micro/macrocephaly, behavioral anomalies, ataxia and speech problems.
FAM160 is a novel ID syndrome gene, which is involved in the etiology of ID, microcephalic, behavioral abnormalities, ataxia and speech problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FAM160 is a novel syndromic ID candidate and should be considered in patients with microcephaly and ID. © 2016 Wiley Periodicals, Inc.

FAM160‐related ID is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder with a broad phenotypic spectrum, including ID, ataxia and behavioral abnormalities.
